title: response contract: tool-call fencing and partial-stream schema validation
author: Daria Chen
description:
Motivation: customers continue to see two pain points when using `response_format` / JSON schema based outputs in streaming mode: 1) partial or malformed streaming chunks trigger tool/function calls prematurely (tool invocation tokens embedded in broken structures), and 2) streaming parsers drop the response when final validation fails without useful, actionable feedback. This PR introduces a small behavioral surface and runtime fencing to address both issues while preserving OpenAI-compat expectations.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a response contract "fencing" layer that defers tool/function invocation until the runtime has validated (heuristically) that the streamed JSON structure contains a syntactically plausible tool_call envelope. This prevents accidental tool activations from transient stream fragments.
- Adds a partial-stream validation pass that runs continuously on the stream buffer and emits non-fatal validation annotations to the SDK and console (validation.hints). Final strict validation still runs at completion and can be configured to be lenient or strict via the new `contract_mode` flag (`lenient|strict|diagnose`).
- Maps new validation and fencing error codes to existing OpenAI-compat error categories so downstream clients (and our OpenAI shim) can continue handling errors in existing flows. See mapping table in docs/openai-compat.md.
- Exposes a `contract_mode` top-level request param. Default behavior remains backward-compatible: if a request includes `response_format` but no `contract_mode`, behavior matches existing runtime (best-effort schema hints, tool calls allowed on first well-formed envelope). Explicit `contract_mode=strict` enforces final-schema acceptance before triggering tool calls and will turn final-validation failures into structured 4xx-style responses. `contract_mode=diagnose` retains behavior plus emits a diagnostic stream of validation hints (non-fatal) to simplify prompt tuning.

Design notes and choices:
- Fencing is implemented as a lightweight state machine inside the streaming runtime: states = {"collecting", "envelope_seen", "fenced"}. The runtime will only transition to `fenced` (and permit tool dispatch) after a syntactic envelope (closing braces/brackets) plus a small set of semantic predicates (presence of required keys like "name" and "arguments" for tool_call) are observed in the buffered stream. This is intentionally conservative to avoid false positives.
- Partial validation uses an incremental JSON/JSON-schema validator (streaming validator) with a capped lookback window to maintain latency. Hints are batched and emitted as a separate `validation.hints` stream event that the SDK surfaces (or logs) but does not interrupt generation.
- To preserve OpenAI-compatibility we maintain the existing `response_format` param shape and add `contract_mode` as an opt-in enhancement. The OpenAI shim translates legacy `format` and `response_format` combinations to `contract_mode=lenient` by default.

Files changed (high level):
- api/server/streaming_contracts.py (new): fencing state machine and streaming validator glue
- api/handlers/respond_v2.py: accept and route contract_mode; minor routing changes for shim compatibility
- sdk/python/redwood/client.py: new streaming hooks for validation.hints events and `contract_mode` helper in request builder
- docs/openai-compat.md: compatibility notes, mapping table for error codes, migration guidance
- tests/test_stream_validation.py (new): end-to-end streaming tests covering fence transitions and hint emission
- examples/structured_tool_calls/contract_mode_demo.ipynb: demonstration notebook for users
- scripts/perf/measure_stream_latency.sh: updated to include fencing enabled/disabled runs

Review conversation (high level snippets):
- Elliot Ramos: "This looks good overall. My only concern is the conservative fence delaying legitimate tool calls in low-latency agents (e.g., 50ms budgets). Can we expose a heuristic flag to relax the fence for low-latency routes?"
- Daria Chen: "Yes — added `fence_aggressiveness` route config (0..3). Default 1 (moderate). We keep it off for `contract_mode=lenient`. Added tests for aggressiveness values 0 and 3."
- Priya Nair: "Docs mapping table is helpful. Please add one migration example showing the shim behavior for existing users relying on immediate tool dispatch."
- Daria Chen: "Added example in docs and an example notebook; clarified SDK behavior (hints arrive as an async event, not as exception)."
- Samir Gupta: "CI flake on test_stream_validation — re-run once with more generous timeouts. Also confirm that memory growth stays bounded with the lookback window."
- Daria Chen: "Adjusted timeouts and added an LRU-like cap on the validator buffer; CI passed on re-run."

CI and release notes:
- CI: all checks passing on main matrix. One flaky test fixed. Additional perf runs show median latency increase of ~6ms with fence_aggressiveness=1; teams can opt out for latency-sensitive routes.
- Release notes: "Add contract_mode request flag to control streaming schema validation and tool-call fencing. New SDK hook `validation.hints` streams diagnostic validation messages; see migration notes in docs/openai-compat.md."

Testing and rollout plan:
- Canary rollout to 10% of hosted traffic for two days with contract_mode=diagnose enabled for internal integration tests. Monitor tool invocation rate (should not increase) and validation.hints volumes.
- If metrics are stable, flip default to include `contract_mode=diagnose` for new response_format requests for 30% traffic. Strict remains opt-in.
- Hotfix path: route-level config allows immediate disabling of fencing for customers who need original behavior.

Rollback plan: automated toggle to disable fencing at route/provisioning layer; immediate fallback to legacy parser if memory or latency regressions exceed thresholds.

release_notes: Introduce `contract_mode` (lenient|strict|diagnose) to control streaming schema validation and tool-call fencing; SDKs receive `validation.hints` stream events; new route config `fence_aggressiveness` to tune fencing heuristics. Backward compatible by default.
notes_for_release_manager: Canary 10% for 48h with contract_mode=diagnose on internal routes. Watch: tool-invocation-rate, validation.hints volume, stream latency P95. Provide opt-out for enterprise customers via route config.
example_request_snippet: POST /v1/responses with body { "response_format": { "type": "json_schema", "schema": { ... } }, "contract_mode": "diagnose" } // SDK will emit validation.hints events and delay tool calls until fence conditions pass
migration_notes: Existing clients get legacy behavior by default. To opt into the new behavior, include contract_mode in requests or set route default. The OpenAI shim maps legacy formats to contract_mode=lenient. See docs/openai-compat.md for examples.
security_considerations: Fencing reduces risk of accidental tool invocation from malformed streams. No new credentials introduced. Ensure policy checks still run at dispatch time. Auditing events include fence decisions for post-incident analysis.
